# Creating a weekly workout plan tailored to your fitness level using AI

**By the end of this guide, you'll have a personal weekly workout plan built around your body, your gear and your free time. This one's for anyone who wants to start training (or restart) but feels overwhelmed by all the conflicting advice online.**

## Before you start
- An account with any major AI assistant — ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Le Chat or DeepSeek all work for this. Use whichever one you already have.
- A few minutes to think about three things: how many days a week you can realistically train, what equipment you have (even "none" is fine), and any old injuries or sore spots.
- About 10–15 minutes total to chat with the AI and tweak the plan.
- One honest note: the AI can build you a sensible plan, but it can't see your body, replace a physiotherapist or track your actual sets and reps. For injuries, chronic pain or medical conditions, please talk to a qualified health professional.

## Step 1 — Open a fresh chat with your AI assistant
Open the AI assistant you already use, either in its app or on its website, and start a new conversation. You'll see a blank text box, usually with a "Send" arrow or a paper-plane icon at the bottom-right. A fresh chat is best because the AI won't get distracted by old messages. If you don't see a chat box straight away, look for a button labeled **"New chat"**, **"New conversation"** or a small **"+"** icon somewhere on the home screen.
💬 Example: not needed — you don't type anything in this step.
You'll know it worked when you see an empty text field, ready for you to type your first message.

## Step 2 — Tell the AI about yourself in one clear message
Type a single message that covers your fitness level, any injuries, how much time you have, what equipment you can use, and your main goal. Think of it like filling in a short form, but in plain English. The more honest and specific you are here, the better your plan will be. After you press send, you'll see a typing animation, then the AI's reply. Usually the AI will either ask one or two clarifying questions or jump straight into a draft plan.
💬 Example: "I'm 38, a complete beginner, no current injuries, and I can train about 30 minutes a day, 4 days a week. I have a pair of dumbbells at home and a yoga mat. My goal is general fitness and to feel less tired during the day."
You'll know it worked when the AI responds — either with a quick plan or a couple of follow-up questions for you to answer.

## Step 3 — Ask for a full 7-day plan with specific exercises
Tell the AI to give you a complete week, with specific exercises, sets and reps — and to include rest days. You'll see a structured response: usually a heading for each day with a short list of exercises underneath. The AI may also break things into categories like "strength", "cardio" and "mobility". If the response is too vague (just "do some cardio"), ask for more detail. If it's overwhelming, ask for a simpler version.
💬 Example: "Great - now please create a full 7-day plan for me. List each day with specific exercises, sets and reps, plus how long each session should take. I want at least 2 full rest days."
You'll know it worked when you see a clear weekly schedule with named exercises, a sensible mix of work and rest, and a reason behind each day.

## Step 4 — Tweak the plan until it actually fits your life
Read through the plan and ask the AI to swap out anything that doesn't suit you. Maybe an exercise feels too hard, you don't have the gear, or a session is too long. Each time, the AI updates the plan inside the same chat — no need to start over. If it doesn't seem to understand your feedback, try being more specific. Instead of "too hard", say "the burpees killed me — can you swap them for marching on the spot?"
💬 Example: "Can you swap the burpees for something lower-impact? My knees feel a bit sore. Also, I only have 20 minutes on Wednesdays, not 30 - please shrink that day."
You'll know it worked when the plan feels realistic — like something you could actually do on a tired Tuesday evening.

## Step 5 — Ask for a clean, saveable version
Once the plan feels right, ask the AI to format it so you can actually use it day to day. A simple table, a checklist or a step-by-step list all work well. You'll see a tidy, copy-friendly version of the plan. Then save it to your phone's notes app, screenshot it, or print it out. Put it somewhere you'll see it before each session.
💬 Example: "Perfect - now can you put this in a simple table I can screenshot? Columns: Day, Exercise, Sets x Reps, Time. And add a 5-minute warm-up I should do before every session."
You'll know it worked when the final plan fits neatly on one or two phone screens and you can read each exercise without scrolling forever.

## Step 6 — Come back after a week and refine
After 5–7 days of using the plan, open the same AI chat again and tell it how it actually went. What felt too easy? What did you skip? What did you enjoy? The AI will then build a tweaked version for week two. This is where the magic happens — the plan keeps improving because it's based on your real life, not a generic template. If you can't find the original chat, just start a new one and paste in your current plan with a short update.
💬 Example: "It's been a week. I did 3 of 4 sessions, the squats were way too easy, and I missed Thursday completely. Can you make week 2 a bit harder on legs and move Thursday's session to Friday?"
You'll know it worked when you have a saved plan you're actually using, AND a smarter version ready for next week.

## Common mistakes
- **Hiding injuries or health conditions from the AI.** The AI can suggest safer swaps if it knows about a sore knee or a bad back. Be upfront. If something is serious or medical, see a qualified professional — the AI isn't one.
- **Asking for an "advanced" plan when you're really a beginner.** It's tempting, but starting too hard is the fastest path to burnout or injury. Tell the AI where you actually are right now, not where you wish you were.
- **Saving the plan and never coming back.** A first draft is just a starting point. The real value is the week-two conversation, when the AI learns what actually worked for you and adjusts accordingly.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** A balanced plan removes the daily "what should I do today?" guesswork, so you actually move instead of scrolling through fitness videos for 20 minutes.
- **For your work or busy weeks:** AI plans can flex around your schedule. You can ask for shorter sessions on meeting days, or for home-only workouts when you can't get to a gym.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't overthink which AI to use. Pick the one you already have. The conversation is what makes the plan good, not the tool.

## Try it now
Open your AI assistant right now and type: *"I'm a complete beginner. I can train 20 minutes a day, 3 days a week, and I have no equipment. Can you design a simple weekly workout plan for me?"* See what it comes back with — then tweak it from there.
